paper.title_en: Properties of strange quark stars in $f(Q)$ gravity: A baryon number density-dependent perspective
paper.abstract_en: We study anisotropic strange quark stars in $f(Q)$ gravity, incorporating a baryon-number-density-dependent bag function $B(n)$ into the MIT bag equation of state, $p=[ρ-4B(n)]/3$. Motivated by a Woods-Saxon parametrization, the density dependence of $B(n)$ provides a phenomenological description of the evolution of quark matter with increasing baryon density beyond the conventional constant-bag prescription. Adopting the Finch-Skea metric ansatz, we obtain exact solutions of the modified field equations for anisotropic matter composed of deconfined up, down and strange quarks. We investigate the thermodynamic stability through the energy per baryon, $E_B=ρ_0/n$, as a function of baryon density and identify the regimes corresponding to stable hadronic matter, metastable hybrid matter and absolutely stable strange quark matter. At sufficiently high densities, $E_B$ falls below the corresponding value for $^{56}$Fe, satisfying the stability criterion for strange quark matter. The resulting stability window, $57.55\leq B(n)\leq 91.55~\mathrm{MeV/fm^3}$, supports stable three-flavour quark matter. Solving the generalized Tolman-Oppenheimer-Volkoff equations, we find a maximum stellar mass of $\sim2.46,M_\odot$, demonstrating that the model can accommodate massive compact stars. The resulting configurations satisfy the relevant causality and energy condition constraints, while their stability is supported by the Herrera cracking criterion and the adiabatic index. These results demonstrate that the combined effects of nonmetricity and a density-dependent bag function can substantially enrich the phenomenology of strange quark stars and provide a viable framework for exploring their internal structure and stability in modified gravity.
